title: Subtracting Integers: Subtract is Add the Opposite
preview: Subtraction-only slice. Anchor with familiar positive-positive subtraction, vary one thing at a time until the surprising 'subtract a negative' case emerges — then formalise 'subtracting is adding the opposite.'

body.goal: Students articulate the rule that subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite, by walking through carefully chosen variations from positive-minus-positive through positive-minus-negative.
body.launch: Quick warm-up on the number-line meaning of subtraction (counting back) so they have a visual anchor. Then start the slice. Don't pre-teach 'subtract is add the opposite' — let step 7 do the work.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up: opposites and the number line.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Edge case — zero is its own opposite.
Anchor on what subtraction has always meant before we mess with signs.

steps.teacherNote: Anchor — both positive, answer positive. Normal subtraction.
Vary one thing: the subtrahend is now bigger. Answer flips negative. Push: 'where is this on the number line?'
Same move, different numbers. Cement the pattern.
Zero as the minuend. Surfaces 'subtraction is direction.'
Switch to a negative start, still subtracting a positive. Both moves push left on the number line.
The surprise. Push hard: 'why is this 7 and not 3?' Don't give the rule yet — let them argue. The aim: subtracting a negative goes RIGHT on the number line.
Same form, bigger jump. Pattern locks in.
Negative start, subtract a small negative. Push: 'are we moving right or left? By how much?'
Same form but the subtrahend's magnitude wins. Answer flips positive.
Edge case: subtracting itself. Confirms the 'add the opposite' framing.
Final repetition with bigger numbers. They should be quick by now.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Repeated subtract-a-negative. Pattern push: equivalent to -3 + 3 + 3.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'In one sentence — how would you tell a 6th grader to subtract a negative?' Push for: 'subtracting is the same as adding the opposite.' Anchor to step 7: 5 - (-2) = 5 + 2 = 7. Have them rewrite three of the trickier steps using addition of the opposite, to make the rule explicit.
